data.name: Botswana
data.summary: Botswana taxes individuals on a source basis: gains on foreign shares are outside the tax, and gains on shares of public or Botswana Stock Exchange-listed companies held at least a year are exempt. Botswana-source gains on other shares and on property are taxed at up to 25% (on 75% of the gain for shares). Dividends bear a 10% final withholding tax; PwC says foreign dividends of resident citizens are taxed at 10%. There is no wealth tax, but a capital transfer tax of up to 5% (individuals) is charged on the recipient of inheritances and gifts, including foreign property received by a beneficiary who lives in Botswana.

regimes.name: Botswana tax resident
regimes.description: Source-based income tax 0-25%; separate capital gains table; capital transfer tax on heirs and donees.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if the individual normally has a permanent place of abode in Botswana and is present at least 183 days in the tax year (1 July-30 June) or the previous one. Non-citizens need a residence and (for work) a work permit.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains are a separate source of income taxed on a separate progressive table up to 25%, but only when the source is in Botswana. Gains on immovable property are inflation-indexed; for other assets 75% of the gain is taxable. Sales of shares of a public company, of shares traded on the Botswana Stock Exchange or of a company that has listed 49% or more of its equity there are exempt if held for at least one year. Gains on foreign shares and foreign property are outside the source-based tax.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Listed/public company shares held 12 months or more: exempt. Taxable share gains: 75% inclusion. Property: inflation-adjusted cost.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Transfer duty on property purchases by non-citizens is 10% up to BWP 2 million and 15% above (buyer-side cost, not modelled).

sources.title: Botswana - Individual - Taxes on personal income

open_questions: PwC's individual CGT table (bands from BWP 36,000) has not been updated to the 2026 personal scale that starts at BWP 48,000; the 25% top rate is the same either way.
Whether the listed-share exemption applies to individuals in exactly the same way as to companies (PwC describes it on the corporate page) was not confirmed in the Income Tax Act.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Domestic listed: exempt after one year (Income Tax Act exemption described by PwC). Foreign listed and foreign real estate: 0, not Botswana-source. Private business (Botswana company): 25% top rate on 75% of the gain = 18.75%. Local real estate: 25% top rate on the inflation-indexed gain.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Regular dealing in shares or property would be business income at the ordinary 25% top rate.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign gains are not Botswana-source and are not taxed.

dividends.summary: Dividends paid by Botswana companies bear a 10% withholding tax, which is the final tax. PwC states that the gross income of a resident citizen includes foreign dividends, taxed at 10%; the treatment of foreign dividends received by a resident non-citizen is not stated and was scored at the same 10%.

sources.title: Botswana - Individual - Foreign tax relief and tax treaties

open_questions: Whether foreign dividends of a resident non-citizen are taxable at all under the source rules (PwC mentions only resident citizens).
dividends.rate_basis: Domestic: 10% final WHT. Foreign: 10% (PwC, resident citizens) with unilateral credit for foreign tax up to the Botswana tax, so treaty-rate WHT of 10% or more would leave no Botswana tax.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 10% on dividends to residents and non-residents; treaties reduce to 5-7.5% for substantial corporate holdings.
dividends.treaty_network: 24 DTAs (mainly southern Africa, plus UK, France, Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg, Malta, Sweden, India, China, UAE, Russia); no treaty with the US.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Companies pay 22%; foreign dividends of resident companies are taxed on accrual; IFSC companies 15% on qualifying international income.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: PwC states there are no property taxes in Botswana; municipal rates in towns were not checked. Transfer duty on purchases: citizens 5% above BWP 1.5 million; non-citizens 10% to BWP 2 million and 15% above.

inheritance.summary: Capital transfer tax (Capital Transfer Tax Act, Cap. 53:02) is charged on the donee or heir on the aggregate taxable value of chargeable disposals received from one donor in a tax year, at progressive rates up to 5% for individuals (PwC, January 2026). Spouses inheriting are exempt; children are not, except for maintenance and education until 21. Property outside Botswana is exempt only if the beneficiary lives outside Botswana.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: First BWP 100,000 of the distributable value of a deceased estate deducted; casual gifts up to BWP 5,000 a year per donee; marriage gifts below BWP 5,000; household goods below BWP 15,000.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Rate bands below 5% exist but their thresholds were not found in an official source; the JSON applies the 5% top rate to the whole amount, a slight overstatement for a large estate. PwC's corporate page gives 12.5% for companies.
open_questions: CTT rate bands for individuals (PwC: progressive up to 5%) were not obtained from the Act or BURS.
Whether a disposal by a non-resident donor of foreign property to a resident child is chargeable.
inheritance.spouse_note: Property disposed of by way of inheritance to a spouse on the death of the other spouse is exempt from capital transfer tax (Capital Transfer Tax Act, Cap. 53:02, s. 4 exemptions; listed by BURS).
inheritance.gift_tax: Same capital transfer tax on gifts (gratuitous disposals), charged on the donee, aggregated per donor per tax year.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Property outside Botswana is exempt only when the beneficiary lives outside Botswana; children living in Botswana are taxed on foreign assets received.
inheritance.domicile_rules: The tax follows the beneficiary's place of living for foreign property; Botswana property is always within scope.

residency.tax_residency_test: Permanent place of abode in Botswana and physical presence of at least 183 days in the tax year (1 July-30 June) or the previous tax year (PwC).

routes.name: Residence permit (non-citizens)
routes.requirements: Non-citizens need a residence permit, and a work permit to work; Botswana has no residence-by-investment programme for passive investors that was verified in this session.

corporate.summary: 22% flat CIT on a source basis; manufacturing companies with ministerial approval 15%; mining by formula (minimum 22%); diamond mining by agreement. Local dividends are not taxed in the hands of a company; dividend WHT 10%.
corporate.special_zones: International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) companies: 15% on approved transactions with non-residents.

sources.title: Botswana - Corporate - Taxes on corporate income

data.us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain fully US-taxed on worldwide income and estates; the app adds the US federal layer. No US-Botswana income tax treaty.
open_questions: No 2025/26 or 2026/27 budget changes to CGT, dividend WHT or CTT were checked beyond PwC (reviewed 9 January 2026).

succession.name: Botswana
succession.summary: A will can dispose of the whole estate: the Wills Act (Cap. 31:04) sets formalities, not reserved shares. A separate Act gives the surviving spouse and family a claim to provision, but not for estates run under customary law. Trusts exist under common law; no private foundation law was found.
succession.family_claims: Succession (Rights of the Surviving Spouse and Inheritance Family Provisions) Act, Cap. 31:03, provides family provision; its s. 3 excludes estates administered under customary law. Details of the claim were not retrieved.
succession.foreign_law_note: No source on whether a resident foreigner can choose their national law. Customary law applies to many Batswana estates.
succession.trust_note: Trusts are recognised under common law and the Administration of Estates Act (Cap. 31:01) deals with property given in trust; no dedicated trust statute was found. No private-foundation law was found.
open_questions: Content and thresholds of Cap. 31:03 not read.
Botswana trust statute (if any) and foundations not found; both answers provisional.
Conflict rule for foreigners' succession not found.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.
Domestic trusts: likely available under the inherited common-law or Roman-Dutch tradition, but no statute or official source was read; confirm before marking yes.
